pr.title: perf(gemm): swap-AB small-M tiles for the SM120 FP8 groupwise GEMM
pr.body:
## 📌 Description On SM120/SM121, `gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` runs one 128×128×128 tile at every `m`. At decode batch sizes most of that tile's rows are empty, and it runs 1.59–1.88× slower than a swap-AB kernel at 1–32 tokens (#8702). This PR adds swap-AB tiles for per-token scales (`scale_granularity_mnk = (1, 128, 128)`): | `m` | Tile | |---|---| | ≤ 32 | swap-AB 128×32×128 | | 33–192 | swap-AB 128×64×128 (epilogue tile 128×32), when it needs no more waves than 128×128 | | otherwise | the existing 128×128×128 | - **Swap-AB** computes Dᵀ = Bᵀ·Aᵀ: the weight goes in the A slot, the tokens in the B slot, and the output is written column-major (n, m), the same memory as row-major (m, n). Scale pointers and granularities swap with the operands; `Sm1xxBlockwiseScaleConfig` builds SFA and SFB with the same formula, so both `"MN"` and `"K"` scale layouts read the same memory as before. This is the same transform `CutlassGroupwiseScaledGEMMSM100LowLatency` uses on SM100. - **Cutoffs 32 and 192** come from a sweep on an RTX PRO 6000 Workstation Edition (188 SMs, 600 W TDP) at a 300 W power limit: the 10 FP8 linear shapes of Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 and Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block, 34 token counts from 1 to 4096, five passes, every CUTLASS swap-AB and non-swap tile that builds. Swap-AB 128×32 is the fastest tile up to 32 tokens on all 10 shapes, and 128×128 wins above 192. The 128/256 cutoffs proposed in #8702 cost 5.7–6.7% more decode GEMM time than 32/192. - **Wave gate.** A fixed 192 cutoff still runs up to 1.17× slower than today's kernel at 112–128 tokens on n ≥ 14336, where the 64-wide token tile needs one more wave. The dispatcher takes 128×64 only when `ceil(tiles_64 / SMs) <= ceil(tiles_128 / SMs)`, with the SM count from `cudaDeviceGetAttribute`. - **No Split-K / Stream-K.** This keeps the PR to tile selection. At 1–32 tokens swap-AB alone reads the weights at 1.28–1.56 TB/s on every shape except n = 256, where Split-K would help (2 CTAs on 188 SMs); that can follow. - **Unchanged:** the 128×128 kernel body (only renamed to `CutlassGroupwiseScaledGEMMSM120Default`), its C = D aliasing and error returns, the `(128, 128, 128)` granularity, `csrc/` and the JIT instantiations. - **Also affected:** per-tensor `bmm_fp8` and `mm_fp8` with the CUTLASS backend on SM120/SM121 use this launcher with per-token scales, so they take the same swap-AB tiles. Before/after on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (188 SMs, 600 W TDP) at a 300 W power limit: GEMM time per forward, summed over all FP8 linear layers of the model, ms, `"MN"` scales, bf16 output, cold L2, CUDA graphs, median of 5 passes. `main` is the prebuilt FlashInfer 0.7.2 module and this PR is built from source; at m > 192, where the code is identical, the source build alone runs 3% faster, so about 3% of each speedup is the build. | m | Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 `main` | this PR | speedup | Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block `main` | this PR | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 27.9 | 15.8 | 1.76× | 33.8 | 17.8 | 1.90× | | 8 | 29.1 | 16.2 | 1.79× | 34.4 | 18.2 | 1.89× | | 32 | 27.6 | 16.6 | 1.67× | 33.3 | 18.4 | 1.81× | | 64 | 28.2 | 19.4 | 1.46× | 34.3 | 22.1 | 1.55× | | 96 | 29.6 | 26.4 | 1.12× | 35.5 | 29.7 | 1.20× | | 128 | 30.4 | 27.2 | 1.12× | 36.3 | 30.7 | 1.18× | | 160 | 45.9 | 40.5 | 1.13× | 51.4 | 44.0 | 1.17× | | 192 | 47.2 | 41.5 | 1.14× | 52.8 | 45.0 | 1.17× | Against SGLang's SM120 swap-AB kernel (`fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm`), timed the same way at 300 W, this PR is within 2% at m ≤ 32 and m = 160–192 and 8–28% faster at m = 64–128. On @AbdullahMadoun's card at its default 600 W the sign of the m = 48–128 band reverses: his table puts this PR 1.17–1.26× over his branch there, and his branch tracks SGLang to within 1%. That is the clock effect in the Reviewer Notes, not a different tile. Any change to that band is left to a follow-up. +    compute_capability = get_compute_capability(torch.device(device="cuda"))
+    if compute_capability[0] != 12:
+        pytest.skip("The swap-AB tile selection is SM120/121 only.")
+    torch.random.manual_seed(0)
+    m, n, k = 96, 4096, 1024
+    tile_size = 128
+    out_dtype = torch.bfloat16
+
+    a_val = torch.randn((m, k), dtype=torch.float, device="cuda")
+    b_val = torch.randn((n, k), dtype=torch.float, device="cuda") / math.sqrt(k)
+
+    if scale_major_mode == "K":
+        a_scale_shape = (m, k // tile_size)
+        b_scale_shape = (n // tile_size, k // tile_size)
+    else:
+        a_scale_shape = (k // tile_size, m)
+        b_scale_shape = (k // tile_size, n // tile_size)
+    a_tile_shape = (1, tile_size)
+    b_tile_shape = (tile_size, tile_size)
+
+    a_fp8, a_scale = quantize_fp8(a_val, a_scale_shape, a_tile_shape, scale_major_mode)
+    b_fp8, b_scale = quantize_fp8(b_val, b_scale_shape, b_tile_shape, scale_major_mode)
+
+    a_dequant = dequantize_fp8(a_fp8, a_scale, scale_major_mode)
+    b_dequant = dequantize_fp8(b_fp8, b_scale, scale_major_mode)
+    ref_c = einsum(a_dequant, b_dequant, "m k, n k -> m n").to(out_dtype)
+
+    c = gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise(
+        a_fp8,
+        b_fp8,
+        a_scale,
+        b_scale,
+        scale_major_mode,
+        out_dtype=out_dtype,
+        backend="cutlass",
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(c, ref_c, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
+
+    c_graph = torch.empty((m, n), dtype=out_dtype, device="cuda")
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        # The warm-up keeps the module build and the workspace allocation off the capture.
+        gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise(
+            a_fp8,
+            b_fp8,
+            a_scale,
+            b_scale,
+            scale_major_mode,
+            out=c_graph,
+            backend="cutlass",
+        )
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise(
+                a_fp8,
+                b_fp8,
+                a_scale,
+                b_scale,
+                scale_major_mode,
+                out=c_graph,
+                backend="cutlass",
+            )
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+
+    for _ in range(2):
+        c_graph.zero_()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(c_graph, ref_c, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["trtllm", "cutile"])
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("m", [4, 128, 256, 512, 4096, 8192])
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("n", [128, 256, 512, 4096, 8192])

Data from a small SM120 part, since the sweep in the description is on 188 SMs: RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (36 SMs, 448 GB/s). PR at `b615721c9` against its parent `ae58183fa`, run base / PR / base (`da31d55aa` since then changes only the error codes and tests, not the tile policy). The two base runs agree within 1.3% (geomean 0.998). Same method as my numbers in #8702: weights kept DRAM-resident (copies covering 8x L2, replayed round-robin in one CUDA graph), median of 30 replays, bf16 out. The shapes are the Qwen3.8-27B FP8 projections per GPU at TP=2, the TP=1 down projection, and two from the issue.

`test_fp8_groupwise_gemm_sm120_tile_selection` passes here (78 passed).

**Before/after, `"K"` scales** (`"MN"` gives the same ratios within 1%):

| M | base / PR | PR, % of 448 GB/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1-32 | 1.16-1.72x (geomean 1.44) | 75-93% |
| 33-64 | 1.14-1.41x | 64-92% |
| 96-256 | 1.00 (unchanged, see below) | 34-81% |

The largest gains are on the N = 5120 layers (down, o_proj: 1.69-1.72x at M <= 32).

**The wave gate on a small part.** On 36 SMs the gate rejects 128x64 at every M from 96 to 192, so those M keep today's 128x128 kernel. For example, at N = 5120 and M = 96, 128x64 is 80 tiles (3 waves) and 128x128 is 40 tiles (2 waves). I removed the gate locally (`if (true)`, nothing else changed) and forced 128x64 for M = 33-192:

| N x K | M | PR (gated) us | 128x64 forced us | gated / forced |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5120 x 8704 (down) | 96 | 215.4 | 163.2 | 1.32 |
| 5120 x 8704 (down) | 160 | 315.8 | 213.1 | 1.48 |
| 5120 x 3072 (o_proj) | 128 | 79.0 | 59.1 | 1.34 |
| 6144 x 5120 | 128 | 131.2 | 99.8 | 1.31 |
| 7168 x 5120 (qkv) | 160 | 251.3 | 156.5 | 1.61 |
| 17408 x 5120 (gate_up) | 128 | 260.4 | 260.4 | 1.00 |
| 17408 x 5120 (gate_up) | 192 | 495.4 | 379.5 | 1.31 |
| 34816 x 5120 | 128 | 519.4 | 523.5 | 0.99 |

Over all 40 points (8 shapes, M = 64-192), forced 128x64 is never more than 1% slower. It is 1.31-1.61x faster at M = 160-192 on every shape, and 1.31-1.34x faster at M = 96-128 on the N <= 6144 shapes. The gate compares wave counts as if a 128x64 wave and a 128x128 wave cost the same, but a 128x64 tile does half the work. From your own number (1.17x for 2 waves of 128x64 against 1 wave of 128x128 at n >= 14336), a 128x64 wave costs about 0.58 of a 128x128 wave. Weighting the waves by something like that keeps your 188-SM case on 128x128 (2 x 0.58 = 1.17 > 1). On this card it would pick a tile within 2% of the faster of the two at all 40 points: it takes 128x64 where that wins (for example 3 x 0.58 = 1.76 < 2 at N = 5120, M = 96, or 12 x 0.58 = 7.0 < 8 for gate_up at M = 160) and keeps 128x128 where the two are level (gate_up and 34816 x 5120 at M = 128). I haven't checked that ratio beyond these points, so treat it as a direction rather than a constant.

**Split-K beyond n = 256 on small parts.** At M <= 32 the N = 5120 layers reach 75-82% here, while the N >= 7168 layers reach 89-93%. That is wave quantization: 40 swap-AB tiles on 36 SMs give 1.11 waves. For comparison, the existing `backend="cutile"` (after its per-M autotune) is 1.07-1.12x faster than this PR on those layers at M <= 32, and level with it on the N >= 7168 ones. So on parts with few SMs, the Split-K follow-up would also help the common n = 5120 shapes, not just n = 256.

Accuracy is unchanged (relative error vs. an FP32 reference 0.037-0.039 on both trees, the FP8 quantization error). I'm happy to rerun on this card after any change.
